title: Generalized tensor normalization implies the geometric-unit equation
statement:
Let $C,D$ be sites small in a common module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $v:C\to D$ induce a geometric adjunction $F\dashv u_*$ on sheaves of sets, with $u_*$ given by precomposition with $v$, $F$ preserving finite limits, and unit $\eta^{\mathrm g}$. Let $R,A,S$ be commutative ring sheaves, with $R$ on $C$ and $A,S$ on $D$. Let $I$ be an algebraic inverse-image presentation of $F$ from $R$-modules to $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image], with underlying identifications $j_X:F|X|\cong|IX|$, and let $\alpha:A\to S$. For every $R$-module sheaf $X$ put $LX=S\otimes_A IX$, using sheafified scalar extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and write $q_X:|IX|\to|LX|$ for $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. Let $P$ be module direct image with scalar restriction along the ring map $c:R\to u_*S$ geometrically adjoint to $F|R|\cong|A|\xrightarrow{\alpha}|S|$, using the ring identification of the presentation. Assume the underlying maps $u_*(q_Xj_X)\eta^{\mathrm g}_{|X|}$ are $R$-linear, and denote them by $\eta_X:X\to PLX$. Let $M,N$ be $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $p_{LM,LN}:PLM\otimes_R PLN\to P(LM\otimes_S LN)$ be the $R$-linear sheaf map induced by the sectionwise pure-tensor pairing at $v(U)$.

Suppose an $S$-linear sheaf map $\mu:L(M\otimes_RN)\to LM\otimes_SLN$ has the following generalized normalization: for every sheaf of sets $Z$ on $C$ and maps $x:Z\to|M|$, $y:Z\to|N|$, $z:Z\to|M\otimes_RN|$ with $z(t)=x(t)\otimes y(t)$ on all sections, one has on all sections of $FZ$
$$\mu\,q_{M\otimes_RN}j_{M\otimes_RN}F(z)
=\operatorname{pure}_S\bigl(q_Mj_MF(x),q_Nj_NF(y)\bigr),$$
where $\operatorname{pure}$ is the section pairing into the sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then, as $R$-linear sheaf maps,
$$P(\mu)\circ\eta_{M\otimes_RN}
=p_{LM,LN}\circ(\eta_M\otimes\eta_N).$$
No module adjunction, lax coherence, invertibility or naturality of $\mu$ is assumed.

proof.text: Take Z to be the cartesian product of the ULift-valued underlying sheaves of M and N. The two projections give x and y. Define z sectionwise as ULift.up of ringedComparisonPure. Naturality of the module sheafification unit and tensorObjIsoSheafification.inv, together with sectionwise tensor restriction, proves that z is a sheaf morphism. Its pure-tensor equation is definitional. This directly constructs the needed pairing without the equal-site-universe restriction of tensor_bilinear_universal.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, Hom/Bilin display following Tag 0GMW; agent choice of the product test sheaf for Tag 03EL.

proof.text: Fix $U\in C$, $m\in M(U)$, $n\in N(U)$, and put $\xi=\eta^{\mathrm g}_{Z,U}(m,n)\in(FZ)(vU)$. Naturality of the geometric unit means $u_*F(f)\circ\eta^{\mathrm g}_Z=\eta^{\mathrm g}_Y\circ f$ for every map $f:Z\to Y$ of sheaves of sets. Evaluate this defining naturality identity for $f=x,y,z$. Since $u_*$ is precomposition, it gives $(Fx)_{vU}(\xi)=\eta^{\mathrm g}_{|M|,U}(m)$, $(Fy)_{vU}(\xi)=\eta^{\mathrm g}_{|N|,U}(n)$, and $(Fz)_{vU}(\xi)=\eta^{\mathrm g}_{|T|,U}(m\otimes_Rn)$.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, third equality; agent expansion using the defining naturality of the assumed geometric unit.

proof.text: Apply generalized normalization to $(Z,x,y,z)$ and evaluate its equation over $vU$ at $\xi$. Substitute the three identities of Step 2. By the stipulated definition $\eta_X=u_*(a_X)\eta^{\mathrm g}_{|X|}$ and the action of $P$ on maps, the left side becomes $(P\mu)_U(\eta_{T,U}(m\otimes_Rn))$. The right side becomes $\operatorname{pure}_{S,vU}(\eta_{M,U}(m),\eta_{N,U}(n))$. Thus these expressions agree for every $U,m,n$.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, third equality; agent evaluation of the assumed normalization at the geometric-unit section.

proof.text: Naturality of the counit of module sheafification and of its monoidal tensorator proves naturality of tensorObjIsoSheafification in both modules. Combine this with naturality of the sheafification unit: tensorHom sends ringedComparisonPure(m,n) to ringedComparisonPure(eta_M(m),eta_N(n)). The assumption hpairing then identifies the right composite on pure sections with the expression in Step 3. To extend equality to sheaf maps, precompose with tensorObjIsoSheafification.inv, apply injectivity of the module sheafification adjunction Hom equivalence, and apply sectionwise ModuleCat tensor extensionality. No assertion that all sheaf tensor sections are pure is used.
